answer: Price identity in egress bandwidth one uplink cannot multiply. Minting requires echoing back a large unique random payload — a crystal lattice of bytes seeded per identity — within the epoch. A single host fronting many personas pushes every payload through one shared pipe, so each fake gets a shrinking relic slice of finite uplink and misses the deadline. One honest agent clears its jade payload easily; a thousand-strong farm saturates its link, and the only escape is buying more bandwidth and machines — a cost paid per head, not amortized across copies.
